readingA.label: A defect
readingA.text: The East is the sun's quarter, and the tradition treats a toilet there as spoiling it.

readingB.label: Acceptable in part of it
readingB.text: The 16-zone school divides the East more finely and allows a toilet in the strip nearest the South-East.

readingA.label: Not ideal
readingA.text: The North belongs to Kubera and the tradition reads it as water, which it does not want set against the kitchen's fire.

readingB.label: Not ideal, but not a fault
readingB.text: Modern practice treats a northern kitchen as less than best rather than as something that needs correcting.

title: The main bedroom in the West

readingA.label: Acceptable
readingA.text: The West is the other settled, heavier quarter, and the tradition accepts it in place of the South-West.

readingB.label: Advised against
readingB.text: The 16-zone school reads the west-south-west as the quarter of study, and keeps the main bedroom out of it.

title: A front door in the South-East

readingA.label: Acceptable in the right position
readingA.text: The 32 named door positions already separate the good ones from the bad within the South-East, so the exact position decides it rather than the direction.

readingB.label: A defect
readingB.text: The Manasara says a home should never face the South-East at all.

title: Which way to sleep with your head

readingA.label: Head to the South is best
readingA.text: The tradition ranks head-to-South first, the East next, and the West as neutral.

readingB.label: Avoid head to the North
readingB.text: The one point every school agrees on. We pass it on as tradition and make no claim about your health.

readingA.label: Against the West or South-West wall
readingA.text: The classical arrangement stands the idols against the West or South-West wall, so the person praying faces East.

readingB.label: Against the East wall
readingB.text: Modern practice often stands them against the East wall instead, facing West.

readingA.label: The sources contradict each other
readingA.text: The North, the North-West and the South-East are each insisted on by serious sources.

readingB.label: Too sharp a conflict to rule on
readingB.text: Choosing one would be inventing a tradition, so we report it as not checked unless you tell us where yours is.

title: A road pointing straight at the plot

readingA.label: It depends which direction
readingA.text: A road arriving from the North-East, North or East is harmless; from the South, South-West, South-East or North-West it is the thrust the tradition warns about.

readingB.label: Always harmful
readingB.text: The strict school treats any road pointing at a plot as a wound, whichever direction it comes from.

readingA.label: A North-East extension is welcome
readingA.text: The tradition treats extra space in the North-East as a good sign rather than a fault.

readingB.label: Every extension is a fault
readingB.text: The strict school treats any part of a home that sticks out as a fault, the North-East included.

title: Where the prayer room belongs

readingA.label: Classical — the centre
readingA.text: The classical position: the family deity holds the centre of the home, as the Manasara sets it out.

readingB.label: Modern — the North-East
readingB.text: Near-universal modern practice places the prayer room in the North-East.

howWeScore: Your score follows the modern reading: the North-East is treated as the ideal place, and the North and East as acceptable. No position is counted as a defect — including the classical centre — so choosing this reading never turns the other school's advice into a fault.
